Header: Casual organism: Peronospora destructor Local Name: Soraj Mukhi ki Rowen dar Phaphondi

Prevention: Downy mildew is a fungus that is wind and seed- borne causing infection of above-ground plant parts and/or when seed is produced by infected plants.
Pathogens can live in soil for 8 to 10 years.
Crop rotation with a 3-4 year break in sunflower cultivation is the best prevention against downy mildew.
To minimize high humidity, plant in the direction of prevailing winds, avoid using windbreaks and manage plant density and spacing, i.e. row to row spacing: 75 cm and plant-to-plant spacing: 25 cm.
Sunflowers should be planted 1 to 1.5 in deep.
Avoid dense stands, poorly drained soils and overhead irrigation.
Do not seed sunflowers in lowlands that flood frequently and that maintain high inoculum levels from alternate hosts.
Monitoring: Rain is not needed for infection.
Check for dews during the night and morning hours as (1.5 to 7 hours of leaf wetness and 6° to 26°C), besides cool and water saturated soil are favorable for development of disease.
White cottony masses (fungal spores) appear on the underside of infected leaves and are a good diagnostic sign of the disease.
Monitoring should be done twice a week when the disease occurs.
Direct Control: The diseased plants should be removed and burnt soon after being detected in the field.
Restrictions: Always wear impermeable gloves, long pants & long-sleeve shirts during spray
Change clothes and wash your hands immediately after applying pesticides.
Don't spray outdoors on windy or rainy days.
Fungicides may be applied on a 7-day schedule, if necessary.
For all fungicides, thorough coverage of foliage is important for the control disease.
Treat the seed with thiophanate- methyl (e.g.
Topsin-M @ 2.5 grams/1 kg seed) while or
Hombre 18.625% FS @ 0.4 ml into 30 ml of water for 1kg seed) to save the new crop from pathogen attack.
Fosetyl aluminium (Aliette 80WP @250 gram/120L water/acre) followed by spraying.
